title: Studio Automations: keyboard focus drops to the page after toggling the flow ledger switch
body:
domain:ui#3 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jV4dWohojjbTJTQq5m

Filing gate: ① user-visible UX defect, stable on screen, landing named (reach: Studio Automations on a fresh showcase, keyboard Space on the flow ledger switch, measured once by the #29139 os-dev).
Business reason: an author who works by keyboard or screen reader turns a package flow on or off for this deployment from Studio's Automations list. After every flip, focus drops to the page body, so they must tab back from the top of the page to find the switch again, and a screen reader announces nothing about where they are. Mouse users don't notice; keyboard users pay on every toggle.
Reader who acts: the ui lane (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/FlowLedgerSwitch.tsx`). Keep focus on the switch across the busy state (for example `aria-disabled` plus a guarded handler instead of `disabled` while busy, or restore focus when the answer lands).
Dedupe: `is:issue ledger switch focus` 126 hits, `is:issue auto-ledger-switch` 531, `is:issue FlowLedgerSwitch` 6, `is:issue toggle focus lost keyboard Studio` 8 (QA runs, epics, #29139 and the closed #28148 / #28570 / #28578, other subjects). No card covers focus on the ledger switch.

Source: found by the #29139 os-dev (PR #29224), not in that card's scope.

## What happens

On Studio → Automations, focus the ledger switch (`data-testid="auto-ledger-switch"`) and press Space. When the toggle's answer lands, `document.activeElement` is `<body>`. This happens on `origin/main` and on PR #29224's branch alike, for a successful toggle and a refused (409) one.

## Mechanism (read at origin/main 49aba82b)

`FlowLedgerSwitch.tsx:61` renders the switch with `disabled={busy || !!walledReason}`. A focused control that becomes `disabled` loses focus to the body, and nothing returns it when `busy` clears.

## Acceptance

- After a keyboard toggle (success or refusal), focus is on the switch.
- The switch still cannot be toggled twice while a request is in flight.
- A test pins `document.activeElement` after the answer; an ablation (back to `disabled` while busy) goes red.
